parts.title: Skyscraper Farming
parts.article:
Skyscraper Farming
 
A Today’s environmental scientists are in no doubt that the world’s resources of fertile soil are rapidly deteriorating, and that new land for agriculture is becoming ever more sparse. Intensive farming, urbanisation, desertification and sea-level rises are all putting growing pressure on the planet’s agricultural land and therefore on food supplies. Currently 24 per cent of the world’s 11.5 billion hectares of cultivated land has already undergone human-induced soil degradation, particularly through erosion, according to a recent study by the UK Government Office for Science.
 
B The global population is expected to exceed nine billion by 2050 — up a third from today’s level — and studies suggest that food production will have to go up by 70 per cent if we are to feed all of those new mouths. This means that scientists will have to develop new ways of growing crops if we are to avoid a humanitarian crisis. Indeed, UN Food and Agriculture Organization figures suggest that the number of under-nourished people is already growing, and with escalating climate change, crop yields in many areas have been projected to decline.
 
C With this in mind, some scientists and agricultural experts are advocating an innovative alternative to traditional farming whereby skyscrapers packed with shelf-based systems for growing vegetables on each storey — known as ‘vertical farms’ — could hold the key to revolutionising agriculture. Columbia University professor Dickson Despommier claims that vertical farming could boost crop yields many times over. A single 20-storey vertical farm could theoretically feed 50,000 people. And if the theory translates into reality as proposed, 160 skyscraper-sized vertical farms could feed the entire population of New York City, while 180 would be needed for London, 289 for Cairo and 302 for Kolkata.
 
D It’s a compelling vision, and one that has already been put into practice in Asia — albeit on a smaller scale. ‘But there are problems, such as initial investment and operating costs that are too great,’ says a spokesman for Japan’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries. Nevertheless, Tokyo-based mushroom producer Hokuto Corporation is a model example of how a vertical farm can be profitable. With 28 vertical mushroom farms operating across the country, it produces some 68,000 tonnes of mushrooms annually. ‘Vertical mushroom farms have more advantages than ground-level farms,’ says Hokuto’s Ted Yamanoko, who highlights the relative cost-effectiveness of his organisation’s farming practices together with reduced emissions of greenhouse gases.
 
E And the impact of vertical farms could extend beyond feeding established urban populations. Despommier sees them as being capable of helping centres of displaced persons — such as refugee camps — in much the same way that Mobile Army Surgical Hospital (MASH) units are deployed in emergencies. ‘Developing an emergency response system for crop production inside specially constructed modular and highly transportable greenhouses would allow for humanitarian interventions,’ he says. ‘If you have three or four storeys of food already growing someplace, they could become mobile units that could be picked up by helicopters and dropped into the middle of a crisis zone.’
 
F But it isn’t only about increasing food production. Despommier is concerned about the harm that farming has done to the world’s landscape over a relatively short time span, particularly the elimination of hardwood forests. ‘Farming is only 12,000 years old,’ he points out. ‘Vertical farming could allow us for the first time to feed everyone on Earth and still return land to its original ecological function.’ Natalie Jeremijenko of New York University agrees. Reducing the land needed for food production could enrich biodiversity, which in turn can raise the productivity of conventional farms. Furthermore, vertical farming could dramatically cut fossil-fuel use and reduce geopolitical tensions in regions where poor farming conditions drive conflict and malnutrition.

analyses.content: 你可能看到“new land”想选和创新有关的选项，但整段的主旨都在强调土壤退化和供给压力这些“problem”。

A段: "Currently 24 per cent of the world's 11.5 billion hectares of cultivated land has already undergone human-induced soil degradation, particularly through erosion, according to a recent study by the UK Government Office for Science."
这段主要介绍了目前全球大量耕地已经退化，农业用地日益稀缺且面临巨大压力，这正是全世界农民都面临的“日益严重的问题（increasing problem）”。
这段提到全球人口激增，粮食产量需要增加70%来喂饱新增的人口，核心就是在讲对食物“不断上升的需求（rising demand）”。
你可能看到“humanitarian crisis”想选紧急救援（urgent relief），但这里的危机是因为人口激增导致大家没饭吃，强调的是长期的“需求缺口”。

B段: "The global population is expected to exceed nine billion by 2050 - up a third from today's level - and studies suggest that food production will have to go up by 70 per cent if we are to feed all of those new mouths."
这段通过具体的数据（例如一座20层农场能养活5万人）展示了垂直农场在理论上极大的“潜在生产能力（Potential production capabilities）”。
你可能会觉得这是在讲原始灵感（inspiration），但这全段都在算一栋楼能产多少粮食、能喂饱多少人，重心全在“产能”上。
C段: "Columbia University professor Dickson Despommier claims that vertical farming could boost crop yields many times over. A single 20-storey vertical farm could theoretically feed 50 000 people."
你可能看到第一句的“problems”想选反对意见（Opposition），但紧接着的“Nevertheless（然而）”引出了本段真正的重点：一个成功的应用案例。
这段以日本的一家蘑菇公司为例，证明了垂直农场已经在现实中有了“成功的应用（successful application）”并且能够盈利。

D段: "Nevertheless, Tokyo-based mushroom producer Hokuto Corporation is a model example of how a vertical farm can be profitable. With 28 vertical mushroom farms operating across the country, it produces some 68 000 tonnes of mushrooms annually."
这段提出可以把垂直温室做成移动单元空投到危机灾区，这正好体现了它提供“紧急救援（urgent relief）”的潜力。
不要因为看到“mobile units”就自己脑补其他用途，“crisis zone”（危机区域）和“emergencies”（紧急情况）明确指向了“紧急救援”。
E段: "'If you have three or four storeys of food already growing someplace, they could become mobile units that could be picked up by helicopters and dropped into the middle of a crisis zone.'"
这段列举了垂直农场能恢复土地生态、丰富生物多样性、减少化石燃料使用等各种“环境上的好处（environmental benefits）”。
你可能看到开头批评传统农业破坏了地貌，但整段后半部分的核心都是在罗列垂直农场带来的各种“环境益处”。

F段: "'Vertical farming could allow us for the first time to feed everyone on Earth and still return land to its original ecological function.' ... Furthermore, vertical farming could dramatically cut fossil-fuel use..."

analyses.content: A段: "Currently 24 per cent of the world's 11.5 billion hectares of cultivated land has already undergone human-induced soil degradation, particularly through erosion, according to a recent study by the UK Government Office for Science."
注意只能填不超过两个词，原文“particularly through erosion”已经点明了具体原因，直接填 erosion 即可。
题目问英国政府研究发现什么是导致土壤退化的重要因素，原文明确指出主要是由于“侵蚀（erosion）”。
题目问垂直农场项目的缺点除了设立费用（setup expense = initial investment）还有很高的什么，原文并列给出了“运营成本（operating costs）”。
题目里有“expense of setting them up”，已经对应了原文的“initial investment”，不要重复填，找后面的并列项 operating costs。
D段: "'But there are problems, such as initial investment and operating costs that are too great,' says a spokesman for Japan's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries."
题目问什么东西可能被用来把农场设施送到食物严重短缺的地区，原文明确说是用“直升机（helicopters）”吊起来空投。
题目需要填一个能“把设施带过去”的交通工具，不要填 mobile units，要填执行运输的复数名词 helicopters。
E段: "'If you have three or four storeys of food already growing someplace, they could become mobile units that could be picked up by helicopters and dropped into the middle of a crisis zone.'"

questions.question: Vertical farming can have financial benefits.

analyses.content: D段: "'Vertical mushroom farms have more advantages than ground-level farms,' says Hokuto's Ted Yamanoko, who highlights the relative cost-effectiveness of his organisation's farming practices..."
题目问谁指出垂直农场能带来财务收益，Ted Yamanoko 明确强调了他们公司农业实践的“成本效益（cost-effectiveness）”。
你可能看到段落前面的 profitable 就急着找人，一定要往后看具体是谁说的话，原文明确把“成本效益”和 Ted Yamanoko 绑定在一起。

questions.question: Traditional farming has had a negative effect on the natural world.

analyses.content: 题目问谁认为传统农业对自然界产生了负面影响，Despommier 明确指出了农业对世界景观造成的“伤害（harm）”。
别和段落主旨（环保益处）混淆，紧扣人名去找，只有 Despommier 在这一段的开头强烈批评了传统农业的破坏行为。
F段: "Despommier is concerned about the harm that farming has done to the world's landscape over a relatively short time span... 'Farming is only 12 000 years old,' he points out."

questions.question: Vertical farming could dramatically increase world food production.

analyses.content: 题目问谁提出垂直农场能极大地增加粮食产量，Despommier 的原话就是能“使作物产量成倍增加（boost crop yields many times over）”。
虽然 B 段讲了我们需要增加食物产量，但具体提出“垂直农场”能大幅增产的专家是 C 段的 Despommier。
C段: "Columbia University professor Dickson Despommier claims that vertical farming could boost crop yields many times over."

questions.question: Traditional farms may benefit from wider use of vertical farming.

analyses.content: 题目问谁认为传统农场也能从垂直农场中获益，Natalie 指出垂直农业腾出土地后能“提高传统农场（conventional farms）的生产力”。
这里的 conventional farms 就是 traditional farms 的完美同义替换，这句话直接跟在 Natalie 后面，非常好定位。
F段: "Natalie Jeremijenko of New York University agrees. Reducing the land needed for food production could enrich biodiversity, which in turn can raise the productivity of conventional farms."
